clue.text: Painful experience in gold trade

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a deal is a piece of trade or business

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a bruising time in the gold business.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial or distressing experience that must be endured.

clue.text: Question a new function for board

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as an engine goes

explanation.surface: Someone queries what a fresh job might be for a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: A quango (quasi-autonomous non-governmental organisation) is a British term for a semi-public body run by appointed members.
explanation.definitionFit: A quango is run by an appointed panel, so it is a kind of board or official body.

clue.text: What nudists might do with jumble?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nudists cast off their clothing, removing it
second meaning: jumble is second-hand garments given away, as at a British jumble sale

explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of donated second-hand goods, much of it old garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded garments that someone no longer wants are what end up as jumble for sale.

clue.text: Cry though hugging partner

indicators.note: hugging means one word's letters wrap around another's

parts.note: THO is the informal shortened spelling of though
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out even while embracing a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's shout on sighting a fox, so it is a call or exclamation.

clue.text: Anglican building flying flag with no end

parts.note: a church is a building used for worship

indicators.note: flying suggests letters tossed about in the air and landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church with a pennant fluttering from it that never seems to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag with no end' tempts you to trim a letter from flag; instead 'no end' is fodder too, and FLAG plus NOEND rearranged gives OFENGLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglican describes or names the established English church and its communion, so the two terms are equivalent.

clue.text: Opener that might be given a turn?

definitions.text: Opener that might be given a turn?

parts.words: Opener that might be given a turn?
parts.note: a handle you twist to open a door; 'opener' and 'turn' suggest a performer or a cricket batsman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' and 'given a turn' suggest a variety act or an opening batsman; the thing actually turned is a round handle on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the round handle that you rotate so that a door comes open.

clue.text: Peak time to get bad American and Mexican food

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A climber at the summit feels sick, like a visitor eating Mexican dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flatbread of maize or wheat, a staple dish of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Empty beer over uniform then laugh, creating commotion

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
haha is the sound of a laugh

explanation.surface: Someone drains their pint over a uniform and laughs, causing a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar, a synonym for commotion.

clue.text: Robin perhaps loves bad luck

parts.note: Robin Hood, the legendary outlaw, is an example of a Hood
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero, so loves gives OO

explanation.surface: A hero like Robin has a soft spot for misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx or run of misfortune, something that brings ill fortune.

clue.text: Alternatively, look up boy or girl?

indicators.note: alternately read, taking every other letter of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suggests checking a reference to learn whether a child is male or female.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair because the name is short for both Louis and Louise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lou is a pet name used for males (Louis) and for females (Louise).

clue.text: Anatole perplexed about name of newborn

indicators.note: about means surrounding, the shuffled letters going around the other piece
perplexed means confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Anatole is puzzled over what to call his baby.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Anatole is not the definition's subject but pure fodder; the surface baby is the real definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal is the medical adjective for the first weeks of an infant's life.

clue.text: Track going round a river — it's something unusual

indicators.note: going round means one piece encircles the others

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track
gives IT; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A racecourse circles a river, and it is a strange sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is a thing seldom found or seen, an unusual item.

clue.text: Insect removed from control to become very angry

parts.note: a fly is an insect
off the means removed from, as in off the shelf
a handle is a control or lever

explanation.surface: A bug is brushed away from a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly off the handle is an idiom for losing one's temper suddenly.

clue.text: Certainly, son will follow you

indicators.note: will follow means this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone assures a parent that the boy will come along after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes is an affirmative reply, which certainly also expresses.

clue.text: Magistrate completely frozen

parts.note: just means completely, as in just right
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: A magistrate is utterly chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice, such as a justice of the peace, is a judicial officer or magistrate.

clue.text: Roughly at odds?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a rough, irregular way
second meaning: odd numbers are not even, so 'at odds' playfully means in a not-even way

explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' usually means in disagreement; the question mark flags the punning reading about odd numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Unevenly means irregularly or roughly, and odd numbers are those which are not even.

clue.text: Peg, one found in home that's the smallest

parts.note: a tee is a golfer's peg

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clothes peg, a single one, turns up at home and it is the tiniest.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeniest is the superlative of teeny, meaning tiny, so it means most minute.

clue.text: Eccentric females stopping union's penultimate strike

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the penultimate letter of union
to beat is to strike
F is the abbreviation for female, so females gives FF

explanation.surface: Women block a trade union's planned walkout, an odd move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action alongside 'union', but it means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or unusual, a synonym of eccentric.

clue.text: Eastern bishop's sin

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An Eastern bishop has committed a misdeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to do wrong or transgress, which is what to sin means.

clue.text: Grab naughty child on ship

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
re means on or concerning
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a mischievous child aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to seize men forcibly for naval service, as press gangs did.

clue.text: Revealed top men working with a poor part of the country?

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Senior men are exposed at work in a deprived region.
explanation.walkthrough: A development area was a British designation for a region of high unemployment given government aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Such regions were officially singled out because of economic hardship, needing state investment.

clue.text: Reply from a king including four different points

indicators.note: including means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king
the four compass points north, south, west and east

explanation.surface: A monarch responds, making four separate points.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a response given to a question, a synonym of reply.

clue.text: Leave the stage once tune changes?

parts.note: ex means former or once, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Performers depart when the music switches.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that actors go off together.

clue.text: Religious school hit new peak

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Buddhist sect reaches a fresh high point.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point or summit of something.

clue.text: Greatly enjoyed dressing to meet journalist

indicators.note: to meet means the pieces join up side by side

parts.note: a relish is a sauce or dressing
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone loved putting on clothes before seeing a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish is to take keen pleasure in something, so the past tense means loved.

clue.text: Anger shown by Pierre every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means only some letters, here every second one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman called Pierre occasionally loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath or rage.

clue.text: Commercial I so need to feature this woman?

indicators.note: to feature means the answer appears within the words given

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a lady must appear in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a female given name, so it names a particular woman.

clue.text: Making notes about end of blaze burning slightly

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece

parts.note: singing is making musical notes

indicators.note: end of means the final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone writes memos about the last of a fire that is scorching things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making notes' suggests writing things down; here it means vocal music.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to scorch the surface lightly, so singeing is a mild burning.
